jobs.description: Purdue University invites applications for a  3 year (12 month FY contract) Postdoctoral Research Associate position. jobs.description: The Global Commerce program at Denison University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the assistant or associate professor level beginning in Fall 2027. Global Commerce takes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of business. The program trains students to think broadly and critically about how global exchanges of goods, services, information, and money shape and are shaped by a wide variety of economic, political, cultural, social, and environmental factors. Students in the program put this training into practice through consulting projects, entrepreneurial pitches, and a variety of co-curricular experiences. The current faculty includes scholars in history, economics, anthropology, organizational behavior, English, and philosophy.We are hiring a tenure-track faculty member from the humanities or humanistic social sciences whose research focuses on questions related to business, trade, or economic life. The hire will teach across our core curriculum, which includes an introductory course on the relationship between commerce and society, an introductory course on how businesses function in the modern economy, an intermediate course centering on a local business consulting project, and an advanced global entrepreneurship capstone in which students develop a business plan. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to develop commerce-related electives aligned with their research area.  (For more details on the Global Commerce curriculum, please see:https://denison.edu/academics/global-commerce.)The teaching load is 5 courses per year, the largest of which is capped at 25 students. A PhD is required by the time of appointment. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to excellence in liberal arts teaching at the undergraduate level, a desire to contribute to the development of the Global Commerce major, and a willingness to work with our colleagues in the Knowlton Center for Career Exploration. Applicants must also demonstrate interest in integrating global perspectives into their teaching and working in an interdisciplinary program. We will consider the extent to which each candidate’s research perspective complements those currently represented in the Department. Applicants must also provide evidence of an active research agenda; continued scholarship is required of all tenure-track and tenured members of the Denison faculty. Additional work experience in the business, government, or non-profit sectors is strongly valued as a complement to academic expertise.Full consideration will be given to applications received byOctober 30th, 2026, though we will continue to accept applications until the position is filled. jobs.description: The American Philosophical Association invites applications for the position of editor(s)-in-chief of theJournal of the American Philosophical Association(J-APA), its flagship research journal.Launched in 2015 in cooperation with Cambridge University Press, J‑APA is now a leading international journal publishing scholarship in all topics, areas, styles, and traditions of philosophy. TheJournal of the APAis a fully open access journal.Professor Heather Battaly, the journal’s current editor-in-chief, completes her term on December 31, 2027. An editor-in-chief or co-editors-in-chief will be appointed in spring 2027, in time for a transition period beginning no later than July 2027. The initial term of appointment is January 1, 2028, to December 31, 2032; this term may be renewed once, for a second five years.J‑APA’s Editor-in-Chief selects and leads a team of associate editors, who recruit referees and evaluate submissions in light of referees’ reports. In recent years there have been six to ten associate editors, but the journal is open to other editorial models under new leadership. The editorial team also relies on the expertise of two dozen internationally distinguished advisory editors, and additional administrative support is provided by CUP. Editorial decisions are made independently of APA leadership. Policies are set by a governing committee made up of the editor(s)-in-chief and representatives of CUP, the editorial team, and the APA’s Board of Officers. For more information, visit thejournal’s web site.The APA provides funding to support the editorial team, and some support from the home institutions of the editor(s) would be welcome though not required. The allocation of funds and nature of institutional support, if any, will vary according to circumstances and will be negotiated with the selected candidate(s).Candidates should be philosophers with outstanding records of research and also with the breadth, energy, vision, and management skills needed to build on the journal’s successes and to continue to set benchmarks for publishing in all topics, areas, styles, and traditions of philosophy. Membership in the APA is not required at the time of application but is required prior to and throughout the term of appointment.Applicants or co-applicants should submit their CVs and a two-page cover letter using theJournal Editor-In-Chief Application Form.The cover letter should highlight editorial experience, if any, as well as any administrative experience relevant to the day-to-day running of an editorial operation. It should sketch a vision of the future of the journal, its aims and scope, in the context of recent trends in philosophy and the publishing environment.Applications will be accepted until an appointment is made, but applications received by December 31, 2026, are assured full consideration. Inquiries about the editorship or nominations of strong candidates may be sent to Marya Schechtman, chair of the APA board of officers and chair of the search committee, at[email protected].Equal Opportunity StatementThe APA will not discriminate against applicants on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected status. Women, racial/ethnic minorities, LGBTQ+ people, people with disabilities, veterans, and members of other underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply.
